description:
Follows the extern-return fold in this epic. `refine_observed_return` (src/compiler2/jobs/semantic.rs:1805-1829)
reads a free type variable two incompatible ways in one function:

```rust
let observed_is_unconstrained = is_equivalent(observed, any) || has_vars(observed);
...
let refined = intersect(observed, contract);
if is_empty(refined) { observed } else { refined }
```

`has_vars(observed)` treats a var-carrying observation like `any` (let the
contract in), then `intersect` treats the same var as a disjoint `vars`-axis
literal (types/descr.rs:135), so `intersect(a0, int)` is empty and the
fallback re-admits `a0`. This is how the extern leak by the extern-return fold survived every
caller's correct contract result.

After that fold no declared variable can reach observed evidence by
construction. Whether the disjunct is then dead is UNMEASURED: activation keys
legitimately carry closure surfaces with vars (`apply1/2[(a0_p0) -> a0_r, int]`,
00549/00550 snapshots), so var-carrying observations may still arrive from
bodies.

## Work

1. Deletion probe: remove the `has_vars(observed)` disjunct (and separately
   the `has_vars(contract)` early return), run the full gate, classify every
   new red (pin improvement / outmoded holder / regression).
2. If dead: delete, with the test that proves a var-carrying closure surface
   still types correctly. If live: name the case in the paper, and make the two
   readings agree (a var is either unconstrained or a literal, not both) --
   decided with the owner before building.

Related seam, out of scope for now: a @spec's declared return refines the
body's return but is never checked against it.
title: refine_observed_return reads a free variable two ways: probe, then delete or reconcile
